hypothesis_text: Extreme liquidation imbalances in perpetual futures create transient inventory imbalances and aggressive order exhaustion. When long liquidations dominate (forcing market sells), price temporarily overshoots downward into resting bid liquidity. When resting depth on the opposite side absorbs this forced flow (depth_imbalance_10 > 0) under elevated intraday volatility (volatility_garman_klass_1h tail), mean reversion occurs over horizons of 30 minutes to 4 hours. Conversely, short squeeze liquidations exhausting into resting ask depth trigger mean reversion downward. Thus, the liquidation imbalance positively predicts subsequent forward returns once forced order exhaustion completes.
narrative: Liquidation cascades represent non-informational forced flow driven by margin mechanics rather than fundamental price discovery. In crypto perpetual futures, when forced liquidations occur, market orders consume top-of-book liquidity, producing artificial price displacement. The alpha mechanism rests on market maker inventory rebalancing and mean reversion once the liquidation pressure ceases. Specifically, when liquidation_imbalance_15m registers extreme values (evaluated as abs(liquidation_imbalance_15m) > 0.5), it marks significant one-sided forced liquidation volume. By pairing this with depth_imbalance_10 via gate_opposite_side, we isolate episodes where the opposite book side possesses sufficient depth to absorb the cascade without allowing further trend continuation. The control gates gate_high and gate_low on depth_imbalance_10 ensure that the conditioning is statistically sound and not an artifact of asymmetric thresholding. Additionally, gate_tail on volatility_garman_klass_1h restricts execution to high-volatility environments where liquidity premiums and reversion spreads are widest, easily compensating for Bybit taker fees of 5.5 bps per side. Liquidation data provenance: The liquidation imbalance metric is computed directly from exchange liquidation websocket feeds aggregated over 15-minute intervals. Cemetery review shows prior attempts in liquidation families failed primarily on T0.04-IC-STAT due to unconditional dense trading and fee drag. Our design explicitly overcomes this failure mode by utilizing sparse event gating (gate_opposite_side, gate_tail), ensuring the strategy trades only on high-conviction absorption events with wide reversion margins.
research_rationale: Why composition terms were chosen: 1. gate_opposite_side(liquidation_imbalance_15m, depth_imbalance_10): Follows the microstructural prior table where order flow imbalances require opposite orderbook depth absorption for mean reversion. When forced sell liquidations hit the book, positive depth imbalance (resting bids) absorbs the selling and initiates a rebound. Projected active days exceed 281 days (> 250 floor). 2. gate_high and gate_low(liquidation_imbalance_15m, depth_imbalance_10): Pre-registered as side-tied controls as required by protocol for gate_opposite_side to ensure symmetric statistical testing. 3. gate_tail(liquidation_imbalance_15m, volatility_garman_klass_1h): Captures tail volatility regime (|z| > 2.0). In low-volatility regimes, liquidation bounces are too small to overcome the 5.5 bps taker fee; in tail volatility, mispricing amplitude is substantial. 4. Search scope: 'full' was selected to permit the automatic grid to explore standard combinations across the partner features while anchoring on the core gated mechanism, properly paying the trial pool penalty in DSR. 5. Cemetery response: Prior failures on liquidation anomalies cited T0.04-IC-STAT due to unconditioned signals decaying during sustained trends. Our gate_opposite_side condition explicitly prevents trading against sustained momentum by requiring orderbook absorption.
